cards.design_implication: If measuring in-plane thermal conductivity anisotropy is required, consider utilizing suspended-pad micro-devices and ensuring the device geometry allows for steady-state longitudinal heat flow along specific crystal directions.
does_not_establish: Generalizability of this specific method to other 2D materials without modification.
Instrument calibration procedures or specific data processing algorithms.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Thermal conductivity measurements were carried out under the condition of steady-state longitudinal heat flow using suspendedpad micro-devices.
limitations: The text supports this method for single-crystal black phosphorus nanoribbons.
The method relies on the specific device geometry described.
cards.statement: Single-crystal black phosphorus nanoribbons are measurable for anisotropic in-plane thermal conductivity using suspended-pad micro-devices under steady-state longitudinal heat flow.

cards.design_implication: If thermal management designs rely on anisotropic properties, these properties may be negligible or significantly different at temperatures below 100 K compared to the room temperature regime.
does_not_establish: The exact onset temperature of anisotropy (stated as 'above 100 K').
Behavior below 30 K or above 350 K.
cards.evidence_excerpt: We discovered increasing thermal conductivity anisotropy, up to a factor of two, with temperatures above 100 K.
limitations: Applies to single-crystal black phosphorus nanoribbons.
cards.statement: Thermal conductivity anisotropy in black phosphorus nanoribbons becomes pronounced at temperatures above 100 K, reaching a factor of two near 300 K.

cards.design_implication: If modeling thermal transport in these materials, the design should account for anisotropic phonon dispersion as the primary contributor to directional thermal conductivity differences.
does_not_establish: Definitive causal proof independent of the specific model used.
The exact quantitative contribution percentages of each mechanism without reference to Supplementary Note 3.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Analysed with the relaxation time approximation model using phonon dispersions obtained based on density function perturbation theory, the high anisotropy is attributed mainly to direction-dependent phonon dispersion and partially to phonon–phonon scattering.
limitations: Based on analysis using relaxation time approximation.
Attribution is specific to the materials and dimensions tested.
cards.statement: The observed high anisotropy in thermal conductivity is attributed mainly to direction-dependent phonon dispersion and partially to phonon–phonon scattering.
